subject: FinBlue: Request for private VPC penetration test details & egress routing assumptions
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <security@finblue.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: sec-ops@finblue.com
Date: Wed, 01 Dec 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pen test evidence for private VPC (peering + egress assumptions)

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security team is preparing the final SIG and CAIQ pack and needs a few clarifications about the penetration test that was performed against our private deployment:

- Did the pen test validate routes across the VPC peering/privatelink we configured (FinBlue -> Redwood private instance)? We need explicit confirmation that the test attempted egress via the peered connection and that peering ACLs were considered.
- Were egress/NAT paths exercised and validated (e.g., SNAT through customer-managed NAT vs Redwood-managed egress)?
- Did the scope include lateral movement attempts inside the customer VPC (pivot from the private instance to mock internal services)? If so, can you provide a brief description of the simulated attack paths and findings (high/medium/low)?
- Any remediation guidance or outstanding remediation tickets we should track on our side?

If possible please share a redacted pen-test executive summary, the VPC diagram showing peering and NAT points, and a simple tracker mapping findings -> remediation owner. Our auditor needs these by COB Friday.

Thanks,
Alex Rivera
Senior Security Engineer, FinBlue

Attachments: none

From: olga.petrov@redwood.com
To: Alex Rivera <security@finblue.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, nikhil.sharma@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2026 09:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pen test evidence for private VPC (peering + egress assumptions)

Alex —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then I'll follow with artifacts and a remediation snapshot: 

- Peering: The assessment included tests that attempted traffic over the peered link. The red team validated connectivity and attempted route-specific filtering bypass; we have the test cases documented.
- Egress/NAT: We exercised both Redwood-managed egress and the customer NAT path in your deployment. The report distinguishes which findings came from which egress path.
- Lateral movement: The engagement included simulated lateral movement from the private instance to a small set of mock internal endpoints (sandboxed, with permission). The goal was to validate isolation assumptions — we ran credential theft and lateral discovery scenarios.

I will attach a redacted executive summary, a VPC diagram with peering/NAT points labeled, and a CSV with the remediation tracker. A couple of clarifying questions before I assemble the pack to make sure we meet your auditor's expectations:

1) Do you require raw exploitation PoCs (screenshots/log snippets) or only redacted descriptions and evidence hashes?
2) For the VPC diagram, should we include host-level metadata (instance IDs) or maintain high-level topology only?

If you can confirm the auditor's preference for PoC detail, I'll deliver the files by tomorrow morning PST.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Security & Compliance Lead, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0126

Attachments: none

From: olga.petrov@redwood.com
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, nikhil.sharma@redwood.com, soojin.lee@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2026 09:34:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Pen test evidence for private VPC (peering + egress assumptions) — quick artifacts request

Team —

FinBlue needs a redacted pen-test exec summary, a VPC diagram showing peering and NAT/egress points, and a remediation tracker mapping findings -> owner by tomorrow morning PST. Auditor asked whether we can include PoC screenshots or only hashes/descriptions.

What I need from each of you: 
- Marissa: Can you pull the redacted exec summary from the December engagement (remove any customer-specific hostnames) and mark which findings relate to peering vs Redwood egress?
- Nikhil: Export the VPC diagram used in the QA review with peering arrows and label the NAT gateways we exercised. Prefer PNG + a short alt-text note.
- Soojin: Produce the remediation tracker CSV (columns: finding id, severity, short description, repro path, assigned owner, status, ETA). If there are outstanding remediation tickets in Jira, include the keys.

Please highlight any items that cannot be sanitized for redaction (e.g., raw exploit scripts) so I can confirm with FinBlue whether hashes suffice. I'm looping you because this will hit the compliance bucket for disclosure.

Thanks — tight timeline on this.
Olga

Attachments: pen-test-raw-archive.tgz (held internally, do not include in customer share)

From: olga.petrov@redwood.com
To: Alex Rivera <security@finblue.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, nikhil.sharma@redwood.com, soojin.lee@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 03 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pen test evidence for private VPC (peering + egress assumptions)

Alex —

Thanks for the patience. Per your auditor preference we are sharing redacted artifacts (no raw exploit scripts). Attached:
- pen-test-summary-redacted.pdf — executive summary with high/med/low findings, mapping to peering vs Redwood-managed egress.
- vpc-diagram-finblue-peering.png — topology with peering, privatelink endpoints, and NAT points labeled.
- remediation-tracker.csv — current status and owners; rows include Jira keys where remediation work is in progress.

Highlights: 
- Peering: Tests confirmed that route tables and peering ACLs prevented unauthorized east-west routing under normal config. One medium finding related to an overly permissive security group attached to a test helper instance — remediation completed 2026-11-28 (JIRA RB-1421).
- Egress/NAT: Both paths were exercised. A low-severity issue was noted where outbound traffic to a metadata service could be proxied if instance metadata protection is not enforced; we recommended IMDSv2 enforcement (remediation in progress, ETA 2026-12-10, JIRA RB-1502).
- Lateral movement: Simulated pivot attempts were contained by the segmentation controls; one low finding described a discovery vector that has been mitigated in the sandbox configuration.

Format notes: We provided descriptive PoC snippets and hashed evidence (SHA256) rather than raw payloads. If your auditor requires additional detail we can redact hostnames to unique tokens and share sanitized logs under an NDA addendum.

Drive link (read-only): https://drive.google.com/finblue-pt-report
HubSpot: HUBSPOT-98765
DocuSign reference: DOCUSIGN-12345

If you want a 15-min sync to walk through findings with the remediation owners, I can schedule for early next week.

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Security & Compliance Lead, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0126
